name: telegram-social-mcp
description: Telegram (social): me, publish_text, delete, publish_image. Every tool maps to a documented endpoint

platform_mcp_telegram_token.title: PLATFORM_MCP_TELEGRAM_TOKEN
platform_mcp_telegram_token.description: Bot token from @BotFather. It is part of the URL path: 'All queries to the Telegram Bot API must be served over HTTPS and need to be presented in this form: https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD_NAME' (https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#making-requests). The bot must be an administrator of the target channel with the right to post (and delete) messages. Same field as the messaging entry (env PLATFORM_MCP_TELEGRAM_TOKEN).

platform_mcp_telegram_chat_id.title: PLATFORM_MCP_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID
platform_mcp_telegram_chat_id.description: The channel (or group) the bot publishes to, sent as `chat_id`: 'Unique identifier for the target chat or username of the target channel (in the format @channelusername)', e.g. @mychannel or -1001234567890; env PLATFORM_MCP_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID. Message ids are unique only inside this chat, so `post_id` values are message_ids of this chat.

tools.name: me
tools.description: getMe: 'A simple method for testing your bot's authentication token. Requires no parameters. Returns basic information about the bot in form of a User object' (id, is_bot, first_name, username).

tools.name: publish_text
tools.description: sendMessage {chat_id: <configured chat_id>, text ('Text of the message to be sent, 1-4096 characters after entities parsing'), reply_parameters?} - 'On success, the sent Message is returned'; `id` is the Message's message_id ('Unique message identifier inside this chat'), so it identifies the post only together with the configured chat. `reply_to` (a message_id in the same chat) is sent as reply_parameters.message_id ('Identifier of the message that will be replied to in the current chat, or in the chat chat_id if it is specified'; the Bot API server parses integer fields from JSON strings as well as numbers, tdlib JsonBuilder get_integer_field). parse_mode is not sent (plain text); no url, and `date` is a Unix timestamp under raw.date, so created_at is not mapped.

tools.name: delete
tools.description: deleteMessage {chat_id: <configured chat_id>, message_id: post_id ('Identifier of the message to delete')} 'Returns True on success' (the runtime answers {status: 'deleted'}; a failure is an ok:false envelope error). Limitations: 'A message can only be deleted if it was sent less than 48 hours ago', 'Bots granted can_post_messages permissions can delete outgoing messages in channels', 'If the bot is an administrator of a group, it can delete any message there', 'If the bot has can_delete_messages administrator right in a supergroup or a channel, it can delete any message there'. A message outside the configured chat cannot be addressed.

tools.name: publish_image
tools.description: sendPhoto {chat_id: <configured chat_id>, photo: image_urls[0] ('pass an HTTP URL as a String for Telegram to get a photo from the Internet ... The photo must be at most 10 MB in size'), caption: text ('Photo caption ..., 0-1024 characters after entities parsing')} - 'On success, the sent Message is returned'; `id` is the message_id inside the configured chat. Only the FIRST image URL is sent (sendMediaGroup, the 2-10 item album method, is not used); further image_urls are ignored. parse_mode is not sent; no url / created_at (raw.date is a Unix timestamp).
